name: Food & Beverage
core_perception: Appetite is decided before reason engages. The category is judged on freshness, craft and the promise of a specific sensory experience, and it is bought frequently at low consideration, so recognisability across repeated exposures matters more than a single perfect execution.
visual_traits: human presence implied through hands and shared settings
communication_needs: make the product physically desirable within one second
state the occasion and the price position clearly
composition: The product occupies the dominant area and is rarely subordinated to type. Compositions resolve fast, and a single hero item outperforms an assortment except when abundance is itself the message.
typography: Legible at a glance with a warm or characterful display voice. Price and offer information must be readable at thumbnail scale, which caps how delicate the type can be.
color: Warm, saturated and appetising. Cool blue and grey suppress appetite response and should be reserved for packaging structure or premium positioning rather than for the food itself.
imagery: Texture is the single most important variable — steam, gloss, crumb, condensation and char. Even lighting flattens food; directional light with real shadow is close to mandatory.
avoid: Desaturated or cool-toned food photography, which reads as stale regardless of how well composed the frame is.
Minimal compositions that hide the product behind typography or empty space when the objective is conversion or promotion.
Overlaying more than two offer messages on a single feed asset, which destroys the appetite response the image is doing the work to create.
